nom: First Aid Beauty Hydrating Sunscreen Milk with Colloidal Oatmeal Broad Spectrum SPF 45

segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin are overwhelmingly positive, describing the formula as deeply hydrating, absorbing without a white cast or greasy feel, and layering well under makeup; one reviewer with dry, sensitive skin, however, could not get past a stinging sensation and a sticky film left on the skin.
segments.sensitive: Most reviewers with sensitive skin, including one with rosacea, report no irritation or reaction and call the formula gentle and calming; a few reviewers, however, had negative reactions, including one whose rosacea flared with burning and extreme redness immediately after application, one who found it stung on contact, and another who returned it because it stung her eyes.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin, including some who describe it as combination leaning dry or combination-to-oily, report it hydrates without feeling greasy or causing breakouts.

concerns.dehydration: Reviewers overwhelmingly describe the formula as strongly hydrating, with several dry-skin reviewers saying they can skip a separate moisturizer entirely and one saying it outperformed mineral sunscreens that left her skin tight; no reviewer reports a drying effect.
concerns.redness: Most reviewers report no burning or redness, including some who used it after a sunburn and found the oatmeal soothing, and one who had no reaction despite using tretinoin; one reviewer with rosacea, however, experienced immediate burning and extreme redness and had to wash it off.
concerns.barrier: The great majority of reviewers report no irritation on the face and call the formula gentle, including several with sensitive or reactive skin; a notable number, however, report the product stings or waters when it gets near the eyes, and one reviewer with rosacea had a severe reaction and had to wash it off.
concerns.blemishes: Reviewers overwhelmingly report no breakouts, including several with acne-prone or combination skin who say it is unusual for a sunscreen not to cause them to break out; no reviewer in this set reports new blemishes from the product.
concerns.oiliness: Most reviewers describe the formula as non-greasy and lightweight despite its dewy finish; a couple of reviewers, however, say it can leave a bit of shine or oiliness that they control with a light layer of powder.
concerns.spots: One reviewer prone to sun spots from photosensitizing actives in her routine reports relying on this sunscreen daily to guard against further sun damage, though she does not describe a change in existing spots.

extraits.titre: A Sunscreen That Hydrates Like Skincare
extraits.texte: Finding a sunscreen that delivers strong protection without drying out my skin can be challenging, but First Aid Beauty's Hydrating Sunscreen Milk SPF 45 checks all the boxes! It's lightweight, moisturizing, and soothing—perfect for my combination skin that leans dry. This formula is more like a hydrating lotion than a typical sunscreen. It absorbs beautifully, leaving my skin soft, plump, and dewy without feeling greasy. Colloidal oatmeal is a standout ingredient—it calms and nourishes my skin while providing an extra boost of moisture. There is no chalky cast, no pilling, and it layers seamlessly under makeup. With broad-spectrum SPF 45, I feel well-protected from UVA/UVB rays throughout the day. I appreciate that it's fragrance-free and safe for sensitive skin, so I can use it even when my skin feels reactive. Unlike mineral sunscreens, this one doesn't make my skin feel tight or dry—it feels like skincare first, sunscreen second. This is a winner if you're looking for a hydrating, non-irritating sunscreen that works well with other products in your routine. It keeps my skin moisturized without clogging pores, and the smooth finish makes it ideal for everyday wear. First Aid Beauty nailed it with this one!
